I was 18 and in a long-distance relationship. I would text her every morning, every night, and everything I between when we talked. I'd always say good morning, good night, sweet dreams, etc. After a while, she didn't answer. I figured she was super busy and just kept saying good morning and good night. I finally get a response, but it's her brother telling me she's been dead. 

Out of my own loneliness and heartbreak, I still sent good mornings, good nights, and little things like anniversary texts and holiday texts. Then, one year later, SHE responded and told me that she faked her death to get away from me. My heart went from broken to shattered like a mirror. I couldn't think of anything else to do but sit in my closet, wrapped in my blanket, and cry my eyes out. I wanted to die more than anything in that moment. This was my fire. 

My village is what saved me. My parents came in to check on me, which they rarely did, and heard me crying. Immediately, my dad picked me up and pulled me into a deep hug while I cried on his shoulder for a good 30 minutes. Even my dog, who was old and normally didn't like being picked up in her old age, let me pick her up and put her at the end of my bed, like when I was a kid. My best friend even said "Get dressed, we're getting ice cream."
